- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing short-term price momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 60+), model often overshoots or fails to peak accurately, then undercorrects.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to anticipate price retracement after peaks.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the final 5–10 days, missing upward momentum or late-stage volatility.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the middle of the forecast window (days 10–20), while true prices often rise or stabilize.
- Model underreacts to recent high prices — fails to adjust forecast downward when recent history shows upward pressure.
- Forecasts are too smooth — lack volatility clustering, especially around mid-forecast period.
- Model tends to overcorrect after minor price drops, leading to false rebounds.
- Model fails to capture seasonal or event-driven price surges (e.g., policy changes, auction results) in the final 5–10 days.
